newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk Southern raises bid for CSX to $10 billion in cash.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk Southern raises bid for CSX to $10 billion in cash.

text.p: Raising the stakes in the escalating battle for Conrail Inc., Norfolk Southern Corp. on Friday sweetened its hostile bid for the big eastern railroad to $10 billion in cash.
The widely-anticipated offer by Norfolk Southern was viewed by analysts as an attempt to ignite shareholder unrest over Conrail's acceptance of a lower offer by rival bidder CSX Corp.
Philadelphia-based Conrail did not immediately respond to Norfolk Southern's latest offer.

On Wednesday Conrail formally accepted a friendly offer from Richmond, Va.-based CSX, which raised its original cash-and-stock bid for the freight carrier to $8.5 billion, which amounts to about $94.44 a share.
Norfolk's earlier bid, which was rejected by Conrail, was for $100 a share, which valued Conrail at $9.1 billion.
Norfolk Southern said its latest offer of $110 a share was superior to CSX's bid because it is not contingent on regulatory approval and will provide immediate cash payment to Conrail shareholders.
"Our increased offer demonstrates our total commitment to this combination," Norfolk Southern Chairman David Goode said in a written statement.

"We are determined to take every step necessary to ensure that Conrail shareholders will have an opportunity to choose between our superior offer and CSX's coercive, two-tiered, front-end-loaded offer," Goode said.
Analysts said Norfolk's offer could pressure CSX to increase its latest bid.
Shares of Conrail were up $2.25 to $95.25 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
